validated_results.title: Serum calcium and the calcium-sensing receptor polymorphism rs17251221 in relation to coronary heart disease, type 2 diabetes, cancer and mortality: the Tromsø Study.
validated_results.reason: The only prostate cancer result is a genotype comparison for the calcium-sensing receptor polymorphism rs17251221 ("The minor homozygote genotype (high serum calcium) had a significant twofold increased risk ... for prostate cancer"), with no population-wide serum calcium estimate for prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Combination of low dose of genistein and daidzein has synergistic preventive effects on isogenic human prostate cancer cells when compared with individual soy isoflavone.
validated_results.reason: This is an exclusively in vitro cell-line experiment treating LNCaP and C4-2B prostate cancer cells with genistein, providing no human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Combination of low dose of genistein and daidzein has synergistic preventive effects on isogenic human prostate cancer cells when compared with individual soy isoflavone.
validated_results.reason: Soy isoflavone combinations were tested only on cultured human prostate cancer cell lines, a preclinical design without incident prostate cancer outcomes.

validated_results.title: Advanced prostate cancer risk in relation to toenail selenium levels.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Prospective case-cohort analysis within the Netherlands Cohort Study reporting toenail selenium in relation to incident advanced prostate cancer with an adjusted hazard ratio and confidence interval.

extraction.comparison_type: highest vs lowest quintile of toenail selenium
extraction.population: Men aged 55 to 69 years at baseline in the Netherlands Cohort Study

sample_size.excerpt: The analysis was conducted in the prospective Netherlands Cohort Study, which included 58 279 men aged 55 to 69 years at baseline in 1986.

cases.excerpt: Complete toenail selenium data were available for 898 advanced (International Union Against Cancer stage III/IV) PCa case subjects and 1176 subcohort members.

effect_size.excerpt: Toenail selenium was associated with a reduced risk of advanced PCa; adjusted hazard ratio for the highest vs lowest quintile was 0.37 (95% CI = 0.27 to 0.51; P trend < .001).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Toenail selenium was associated with a reduced risk of advanced PCa; adjusted hazard ratio for the highest vs lowest quintile was 0.37 (95% CI = 0.27 to 0.51; P trend < .001).

design.excerpt: The study employed a case-cohort design for which a random subcohort was sampled at baseline.

timing.excerpt: Incident advanced PCa case subjects from the entire cohort were identified during 17.3 years of follow-up.

continent.excerpt: a population from the Netherlands where low selenium status is widespread

exposure_measurement.excerpt: participants provided toenail clippings, which were used for toenail selenium measurements using instrumental neutron activation analysis

validated_results.reason: Alcohol use is only listed among nine dichotomous variables examined in BRCA mutation families, and no alcohol-specific prostate cancer incidence estimate is separable from the reported aspirin, exercise, and coffee findings.

validated_results.title: Lycopene/tomato consumption and the risk of prostate cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective studies.
validated_results.journal: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology
validated_results.reason: The article is a "systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective studies" pooling eleven cohort and six nested case-control studies rather than original data.

validated_results.title: Lycopene/tomato consumption and the risk of prostate cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective studies.
validated_results.journal: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology
validated_results.reason: Tomato intake odds ratios are pooled meta-analytic estimates from previously published studies, not an original human study.
